info.bio:
Joni Mitchell (nacida como Roberta Joan Anderson el 7 de noviembre de 1943, en Alberta) es una músico y pintora canadiense. Comenzó su carrera musical en Toronto y en el oeste de Canadá, relacionándose posteriormente con la floreciente escena de folk de Nueva York de mediados de los sesenta. A lo largo de los años 70 amplió sus horizontes musicales, dirigiendo en especial su interés hacia el pop y el jazz, para convertirse en una de las cantantes y compositoras más respetadas de finales del siglo XX. Mitchell es también una exitosa artista plástica; las portadas de casi todos sus álbumes han sido creadas por ella misma. Insiste a menudo en que la pintura era su vocación original, autodescribiéndose como una "pintora descarrilada por las circunstancias".

Mitchell puede ser considerada una "música de los músicos"; su obra ha tenido una enorme influencia en una gran cantidad de artistas; no sólo ha influenciado a cantautores similares como Sheryl Crow y Shawn Colvin, sino a un número importante de artistas en diversos géneros, como K.D. Lang, Elvis Costello, PM Dawn, Janet Jackson, Agnes Chan, y Prince. 

Aunque Mitchell usualmente evita hablar sobre otros artistas, en especial de aquellos a los que influenció, ella ha quedado impresionada por dos artistas de jazz que interpretaron parte de su obra, Cassandra Wilson y Diana Krall. Aunque la mayoría de los oyentes tienden a recordar los éxitos tempranos de Mitchell (de sus álbumes más comerciales), muchos músicos se inspiraron en sus trabajos más experimentales, particularmente en The Hissing of Summer Lawns y Hejira.

scenes.name: Charles Mingus
scenes.author: Ted Gioia
scenes.desc: Un castillo de naipes de influencias (Ellington, Bird, el cool y Tristano, el free, Strauss y Bach) convertido en estilo personal: el «estilo sin estilo» que luego sería norma, aprendido de primera mano con Armstrong, Ellington, Parker, Tatum o Powell. Contrabajista a lo Blanton y compositor, sus Jazz Workshops de finales de los cincuenta (Pithecanthropus Erectus, Mingus Ah Um, Blues & Roots) son una iglesia santificada en mil lenguas: gospel y blues, contrapunto que evoca un Dixieland surrealista, cambios bruscos de tempo, piezas enseñadas de oído y despidos en mitad del concierto. Con Eric Dolphy y Roland Kirk se acerca al free sin entregarse; The Black Saint and the Sinner Lady (1963) es su obra extensa más lograda, y el concierto del Town Hall de 1962, un fiasco que Schuller reconstruyó como Epitaph. Para Gioia, el Ezra Pound del jazz: fragmentos ante sus ruinas, crisis psiquiátricas, desahucios y un regreso en los setenta con George Adams y Don Pullen.
scenes.family: Hard bop, soul jazz y post-bop

scenes.name: Voces del jazz moderno: Ella, Sarah, Carmen y el vocalese
scenes.author: Ted Gioia
scenes.desc: La faceta más ligada a la tradición del jazz de los setenta y ochenta. Norman Granz convierte a Ella Fitzgerald, ya superventas desde la banda de Chick Webb, en una artista mayor con los songbooks dedicados a Porter, Gershwin, Arlen, Ellington y Berlin y los directos de Berlín y Roma; en Pablo la empareja con Basie o Joe Pass. Carmen McRae y Betty Carter prolongan a Billie Holiday con libertades rítmicas casi vanguardistas; Sheila Jordan y Mel Tormé siguen sus propios caminos. El vocalese de Eddie Jefferson y Jon Hendricks pone letra a solos famosos y convierte al cantante en un griot que narra la historia del jazz (Joni Mitchell con «Goodbye Pork Pie Hat», Manhattan Transfer). Bobby McFerrin, imitador de metales y director de orquesta, triunfa con «Don't Worry, Be Happy» y se niega a explotar el éxito.
scenes.family: Piano y voces: stride, boogie y cantantes

scenes.name: Carreras en solitario: cantautores de finales de los sesenta
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Los excéntricos de Los Ángeles (David Axelrod, cuyos breakbeats orquestales anticipan el trip-hop; Van Dyke Parks y su música de cámara pop; David Ackles, Kim Fowley, Wild Man Fischer) y los herederos del Greenwich (Laura Nyro, Eric Andersen, David Peel, Angus MacLise y Nico, cuyas letanías fúnebres inventan el rock gótico casi por accidente: Marble Index, Desert Shore). Canadá aporta a Leonard Cohen, Gordon Lightfoot, Joni Mitchell (Blue, Hejira) y Neil Young, que con Dylan y Springsteen forma la gran tríada «moral» de la música americana e inventa la guitarra distorsionada que influirá en el grunge. En Texas, Townes Van Zandt; en Gran Bretaña, Scott Walker, Nick Drake (Pink Moon), Roy Harper, John Martyn, Cat Stevens, Rod Stewart, Eric Burdon y Jack Bruce.

podcast.title: Move to United States (1965)
podcast.body: Joni Mitchell relocated to the United States in 1965, becoming an integral part of the Laurel Canyon music scene in Los Angeles, which was a hub for folk and rock musicians. "Joni Mitchell moved to the United States in 1965 and she was part of the whole Laurel Canyon scene in LA."

podcast.body: Joni Mitchell was one of the significant Canadian artists who, prior to 1970, relocated to the United States to pursue a viable career in music, due to the underdeveloped Canadian music infrastructure. "Neil Young, Jody Mitchell, Paul Anke, Leonard Cohen, all of our biggest and most promising artists beat a path for the United States."

podcast.title: Childhood Polio Infection
podcast.body: Joni Mitchell contracted polio in 1951 when she was nine years old. The disease caused her spine to become twisted, and she was unable to walk. She spent weeks in the hospital and was bedridden for months afterward, but she pushed herself to walk again, motivated by not wanting to miss Christmas. "Joni Mitchell caught polio in 1951 when she was nine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Ambition and Canadian Success
podcast.body: In a 1979 interview with Cameron Crowe, Joni Mitchell recalled that early Canadian artists, including Neil Young, had modest aspirations, with Young reportedly aiming for enough money to buy "a purse and a chicken farm." She stated that none of them had "grandiose ideas" about the scale of success they eventually achieved, considering it "a long shot," particularly for a Canadian artist. "none of us had any grandiose ideas about the kind of success we received in those days it was really a long shot especially for a Canadian."

podcast.title: Flow to America
podcast.body: Joni Mitchell was among the ambitious and talented Canadian musicians who flowed south to seek their fortune in America. This movement was characteristic of an era when Canadian artists often needed external validation, particularly from the United States, to gain full acceptance in their home country. "ambitious, talented Canadian musicians flowed south to seek their fortune in America."

podcast.title: Impact of Polio on Music
podcast.body: The polio infection left Joni Mitchell with some mobility problems in her left hand, which unexpectedly proved to be a creative advantage. This limitation compelled her to form chords in innovative and interesting ways, leading to her unique guitar technique. There are now entire websites dedicated to her distinct playing style, directly influenced by her polio. "The polio left her with some mobility problems in her left hand."

podcast.title: Muse-Driven Artist with Concentrated Hits
podcast.body: Joni Mitchell consistently followed her muse into unusual corners and scored more hits than Lou Reed or Neil Young. However, her major hits were concentrated in the early 1970s, unlike David Bowie, who maintained a presence in the Top 40 over multiple decades. "She certainly followed her muse into unusual corners."

podcast.title: Musical Origin – Piano to Guitar at 20
podcast.body: Joni Mitchell initially played the piano and did not acquire her first guitar until she was 20 years old. Many of her early songs were composed on a dulcimer. "Joni was a piano player, didn't buy her first guitar until she was 20."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Polio's Influence on Guitar Technique and Tunings
podcast.body: A childhood bout with polio resulted in a weakened left hand, compelling Joni Mitchell to invent creative chord voicings. This led to her extensive use of unusual guitar tunings, reportedly employing at least 51 different tunings throughout her career. "And because about of polio left her with a weakened left hand, she had to be creative with how she formed chords and that led to all kinds of exotic tunings."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Polio Syndrome and Later Afflictions
podcast.body: At age 51, decades after her initial recovery, Joni Mitchell experienced the resurgence of her polio symptoms in the form of post-polio syndrome, a condition affecting up to 40% of patients. She has also battled Morgellons disease, a rare condition characterized by fibers appearing under the skin, which nearly halted her recording and performing career multiple times. "At age 51, it all came roaring back as post polio syndrome, which effects up to 40% of patients' decades after they thought they'd recovered."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Shift to Folk from "Vanilla" Rock
podcast.body: Joni Mitchell explained that she gravitated towards folk music because the post-Chuck Berry, post-Elvis rock of her era had become "vanilla," lacking the depth or originality she sought. "Joni Mitchell who said she turned to folk when kind of post Chuck Berry post Elvis rock became as she described it vanilla."

podcast.title: Unique Guitar Style – Melodic and Percussive
podcast.body: Joni Mitchell's signature guitar style was characterized by a right-hand technique that combined melodic and percussive elements. Her playing incorporated unique tunings, unusual chords, harmonics, and percussive sounds, making her a distinctive voice among guitarists. "She also had a special way of stroking the strings with her right hand that could be both melodic and percussive at the same time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Apology and Compliment to The Trews
xref.body: After his initial displeasure regarding The Trews' "Bohemian Rhapsody" cover, Robert Plant later offered a subtle apology during a show in Calgary at the Saddledome. He publicly acknowledged Canada's rich songwriting history, mentioning Neil Young, Joni Mitchell, and Leonard Cohen, and significantly, included "the trues" in this esteemed list. "Canada has always had such a rich history of songwriting and with Neil Young and Joni Mitchell and Leonard Cohen and the trues. And I took that as his his apology for telling us."

xref.title: Early Career and Discovery
xref.body: Before his breakthrough, Tom Waits worked as a doorman at a nightclub in San Diego that featured "idiosyncratic performers." He drew the attention of Asylum Records due to his early folk and jazzy style, reminiscent of Joni Mitchell. The label's founders, David Geffen and Elliot Roberts, who were fans of Bob Dylan, saw Waits as a potential "Dylan" for their roster. "Tom caught the attention of Asylum because like the other artists on the label, he was sort of foky at the beginning."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Career as Doorman and Asylum Signing
xref.body: Before gaining attention from Asylum Records, Tom Waits worked as a doorman at a nightclub in San Diego known for featuring idiosyncratic performers. He caught the attention of Asylum because his early work had folk and jazzy elements, similar to other artists on the label like Joni Mitchell. David Geffen and Elliot Roberts, fans of Bob Dylan, saw Waits as potentially their own "Dylan" and were open to experimenting with him, especially given the popularity of the California singer-songwriter scene in the 1970s. "He'd been working as a door man at a nightclub in San Diego that liked to feature some, well, idiosyncratic performers of the day."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Frankenmuth Hometown and Musical Upbringing
xref.body: The Kiszka brothers grew up in Frankenmuth, central Michigan, a town of approximately 5,000 residents whose main attraction is the "world's largest Christmas store." Their parents exposed them to classic rock and blues music, including artists like Led Zeppelin, Jimi Hendrix, Joni Mitchell, and 30s/40s folk and blues legends like Muddy Waters and Robert Johnson. "They're really from the middle of nowhere, a central Michigan town called Frankenmuth. In about 5,000, the biggest attraction is the self-proclaimed world's largest Christmas store. This is where the Kiska family grew up."

xref.title: Musical Development and Hard Rock Focus
xref.body: By 1967, Nancy and Ann were performing as The Viewpoints, with Nancy also doing solo shows influenced by Joni Mitchell and Paul Simon, as well as rock figures like John Lennon, Paul McCartney, Jimi Hendrix, and Jimmy Page. As their groups evolved into Heart, Nancy increasingly focused on hard rock and discovered drop D tuning, a technique that would become vital to the grunge era 15 years later. "By the time some of the various groups she was in with Ann evolved into Hart, Nancy had become much more focused on hard rock and she discovered drop D tuning, something that would become essential to the grunge era 15 years later."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Nurturing Musical Environment
xref.body: The Kiszka brothers were raised in a "musically nurturing environment" that extended beyond just music to include film and literature. They were surrounded by traditional music, including early American blues artists like Elmore James, Willie Dixon, Robert Johnson, Muddy Waters, and Howlin' Wolf, as well as folk artists like Arlo Guthrie, Bob Dylan, Joni Mitchell, and John Denver, primarily from their parents' vinyl collection. "we were kind of raised in a musically nurturing environment where it wasn't necessarily just music, but there was a lot of film and a lot of literature. And we had a lot of traditional music, you know, lying around."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Unique Playing Technique
xref.body: Ani DiFranco is characterized by a "passive aggressive" playing style, utilizing various open tunings and often taping finger picks to her right-hand fingers. Her acoustic guitar technique is highly percussive, and her vocal melodies, which "dance around" the guitar, draw comparisons to Joni Mitchell. "Ani has a passive aggressive style of playing. She uses all sorts of open tunings and often wears finger picks that she tapes to the fingers of her right hand. The guitar might be acoustic, but she's always finding ways to make things more percussive. And the way her vocal melodies dance around a guitar might make you think a little bit of Joni Mitchell."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Versatile Session Musician
xref.body: Beyond Motown, Bobby Jean Hall has an impressive client list that includes a diverse range of legendary artists. Her percussion work has graced albums by Bob Dylan, Lynyrd Skynyrd, Rod Stewart, Janis Joplin, Joni Mitchell, Dolly Parton, The Doobie Brothers, Aretha Franklin, Tracy Chapman, James Taylor, and Stevie Nicks, highlighting her status as a highly sought-after session player. "Other clients have included Bob Dylan, Leonard Skinner, Rod Stewart, Janice Joplin, Joni Mitchell, Dolly Parton, The Dooby Brothers, Aretha Franklin, Tracy Chapman, James Taylor, and Stevie Nicks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Yorkville Folk Scene Pioneer
xref.body: In the 1960s, she developed her skills as a singer-songwriter and was a regular presence in Toronto's Yorkville District folk scene, alongside other emerging talents like Neil Young, Leonard Cohen, Joni Mitchell, and John Kay. "In the 1960s, she developed as a singer-songwriter in Hangout and Toronto's Yorkville District at the same time as Neil Young and Leonard Cohen and Joni Mitchell and John Kaye, who would later form Steppenwolf and many others."
